name: EXACT (Explainable AI Comparison Toolkit)
description: The evolving landscape of explainable artificial intelligence (XAI) aims to improve the interpretability of intricate machine learning (ML) models, yet faces challenges in formalisation and empirical validation, being an inherently unsupervised process. In this paper, we bring together various benchmark datasets and novel performance metrics in an initial benchmarking platform, the Explainable AI Comparison Toolkit (EXACT), providing a standardised foundation for evaluating XAI methods. Our datasets incorporate ground truth explanations for class-conditional features, and leveraging novel quantitative metrics, this platform assesses the performance of post-hoc XAI methods in the quality of the explanations they produce. Our recent findings have highlighted the limitations of popular XAI methods, as they often struggle to surpass random baselines, attributing significance to irrelevant features. Moreover, we show the variability in explanations derived from different equally performing model architectures. This initial benchmarking platform therefore aims to allow XAI researchers to test and assure the high quality of their newly developed methods.
evaluation_method: F1 / AUPRC / IoU (overlap/correlation between produced explanations and ground-truth explanations)
typical_sota_score: near-random / low (varies widely; many methods reported struggling to outperform random baselines, e.g., low tens of percent)
reputation: Early-stage, research-focused toolkit cited by XAI researchers but not yet widely adopted as a community standard.
notes: Small, research-oriented collection with synthetic and curated ground-truth explanations; metric choice strongly affects conclusions; evaluates post-hoc XAI (non-LLM-specific); variability across model architectures; potential sensitivity to dataset design.
